concepts.definition: Explicit sensitive capability authorization decision; not provider role or membership.

relationships.meaning: Enterprise governance rechecks IdentityAccess authorization decisions in the caller transaction from Enterprise-owned EnterpriseOwner facts and current qualification; IdentityAccess does not write the EnterpriseOwner lifecycle.

Account User administration rechecks IdentityAccess decisions for users.read, users.suspend, and last-permission-administrator protection; Account retains User lifecycle, status, version, and replay authority.

Organization governance rechecks IdentityAccess authorization decisions in the caller transaction for Owner-controlled lifecycle, Owner appointment, and member creation policy; IdentityAccess does not write OrganizationOwner facts.
Repository consumes current IdentityAccess authorization decisions for Repository-owned access and protected operations; IdentityAccess does not own or mutate Repository grant truth.
Team resolves the verified request actor through IdentityAccess; Account still owns User qualification, while Team and Organization own TeamMaintainer and OrganizationOwner authorization decisions.

Audit reads a minimal governance event projection for an exact active Enterprise or Organization scope after current owner authorization; no private history access or source-object authority transfers.

capabilities.intent: Decide current scoped feature permission without treating identity or membership as authorization.

implementation.scope: current Identity Access permission application surface
implementation.note: Permission source, exports and transaction/authorization tests are present. PostgreSQL multi-session execution requires the disposable CI service; provider/device acceptance remains separate.
